items.reported: Switching the VIEW dropdown between Pilot health, State readiness and Research detail takes a very long time (the morning's ADM-2 was the state dropdown; this is the view dropdown).
items.correctState: The choice is acknowledged the instant it is made with a status line (already so since ADM-2), and the server render behind it makes one round of reads: the research page issued six reads, then the fleet, then the window, then its incidents — four sequential trips to Neon on every switch.
items.checkId: tests/admin-feedback-9-4-pm.test.ts::ADM-14: the research page issues its reads in one round and the header still acknowledges the choice at once
items.checkResult: MEASURED on the local production build against the real control plane (Playwright, warm server, two runs): the choice is acknowledged in 29–45 ms and the new view renders in 369–423 ms (State readiness), 778–788 ms (Pilot health) and 1,134–1,519 ms (Research detail); a cold first load of /admin was 3.2–3.4 s. The three sequential waits on /admin/research (readWorkerFleet, readLastWindow, and the snapshot read the page now needs for names) joined the single Promise.all; the header's transition and pending line are unchanged. What this cannot fix is a Netlify function cold start in production, which is not measured here and is named as such.

items.reported: The ZIP table says where each ZIP stands (63%, not complete, worst-of blocked, least-ready body) and never what to do about it.
items.correctState: Every ZIP row carries a next step one step past what the row already knows — 'Go get this one thing: <least-ready body>' for a blocked body, 'Nobody has looked yet' for an unwalked one, 'Refresh' for a stale one, 'Waiting on you' for an operator-gated one — and a Deploy-fleet-here button that records a DISPATCH intent aimed at that ZIP and returns to the state's page.
items.checkId: tests/admin-feedback-9-4-pm.test.ts::ADM-15: readiness says the next thing to do, and a Deploy-fleet-here control carries its own target
items.checkResult: GREEN — re-pointed 2026-09-23 to the owner's Meanwhile Admin design, which replaces the per-ZIP table: All states says the next thing to do for each state, from its own gaps; each district, county or metro names the worst gap inside it; an opened one lists every code's standing, and Deploy fleet here opens the Work composer with that geography already chosen, showing what sending does before anything moves. Rendered locally against the production stores (read-only) for Arizona. (Before: NextStep in the readiness panel and a per-row Deploy-fleet intent returning to /readiness/<state>.)

items.reported: The decision cards claim an answer is recorded at once and carried into the tracker at the next sync; the owner asks where his answer actually goes, whether the tracker updates and whether the row leaves — and nothing scheduled the sync.
items.correctState: Recording an answer moves the card out of 'waiting on you' at once into a decided list carrying a three-step receipt — recorded, closed in the tracker (as docs/tracker-resolved.csv#<row>), work opened (DEC rows by id and title) — each read live from the decision log; the sync runs unattended on the standing runner after every cycle, before it republishes the console.
items.checkId: tests/admin-feedback-9-4-pm.test.ts::ADM-16: the whole way out, on a file-backed control plane: record → pull → the applied tracker rows → canonicalize → a receipt with every step DONE
items.checkResult: GREEN — the four legs the owner named: (1) lib/control-plane/decision-receipt.ts splits decided cards out of the count and derives the receipt; (2) scripts/canonicalize-owner-decisions.mts records the resolved row and (3) the DEC rows opened (openedWork, subjectTitle) on the #resolved twin; (4) scripts/apply-owner-decisions.mts runs pull → tracker:move --only=dashboard → canonicalize and is registered in scripts/pilot-runner.mts CONSOLE_PUBLISHERS ahead of the snapshot. Proved end to end on a file-backed control plane in the cited test; the runner's first live application happens on its next cycle after this merges and the main checkout is fast-forwarded.

items.checkId: tests/admin-feedback-9-4-pm.test.ts::ADM-17: a role whose attempts all ran without a paid model is $0 by design with its non-dollar measures; a model role with no dollars is unmeasured
items.checkResult: GREEN — lib/control-plane/cost-panel.ts decides MEASURED / FREE_BY_DESIGN / UNMEASURED from each attempt's worker identity, never by assumption, and sums requests, bytes and duration per role; the publisher adds spendByDay over the trailing fortnight. The owner's note that measurement work may be in another code session: no such change exists on main or any open branch at e88de917; nothing was duplicated.
